x.Wearable Sensor Accuracy: Precision of physiological measurements (e.g., heart rate, ECG, glucose) in real-world conditions; evidenced by clinical studies and independent validation.
x.Device Portfolio Breadth: Range of wearable devices offered (e.g., fitness trackers, medical-grade monitors, patches) covering multiple indications; evidenced by product lineup and FDA clearances.
x.Clinical Validation & Evidence: Strength of clinical evidence supporting device accuracy and health outcomes; evidenced by peer-reviewed publications and regulatory approvals.
x.Battery Life & Form Factor: Battery longevity and wearability (size, weight, comfort) affecting user compliance; evidenced by product specs and user reviews.
x.Data Integration & Interoperability: Ability to integrate with EHRs, APIs, and other health platforms; evidenced by partnerships with health systems and interoperability certifications.

y.Regulatory Approvals & Clearances: Number and scope of FDA, CE, or other regulatory approvals for medical use; evidenced by official registrations and product labels.
y.Market Penetration & Adoption: Extent of adoption by consumers and healthcare providers; evidenced by sales volumes, market share, and clinical deployment.
y.Reimbursement & Payer Coverage: Level of insurance coverage and reimbursement codes for the device; evidenced by payer policies and inclusion in formularies.
y.Revenue Growth & Profitability: Financial performance including revenue growth rates and margins; evidenced by financial reports and earnings calls.
y.Strategic Partnerships & Ecosystem: Collaborations with pharma, tech, or healthcare organizations that expand market reach; evidenced by press releases and joint ventures.

xy_scoring.axis_definition_reason: These parameters capture the dual nature of wearable medical devices: they must be clinically accurate and validated (X) while achieving commercial success through regulatory, reimbursement, and market adoption (Y).
